nokeepai: merge its rank-64 LoRA into the IQ4_NL (tools/merge_lora.py) and it runs at base speed, 29.0.
LoRA at runtime costs 7% (nokeepai) and 26% (AtomicChat).

Needles 3/3 at 32k and 62k. Image input works.

inkling-2-mini-uncensored-results-light.png
Results card: Inkling-2-Mini, uncensored, on a 12 GB RTX 3060 with AtomicChat's AD-Q4_K at 64k context. Refusal probe answered 8 of 20 unedited, 20 of 20 edited; decode 29.0 to 29.6 tok/s; KLD against Q8_0 0.0085 to 0.014. A table of five variants (tok/s, KLD, probe): unedited 29.0, 0.0085, 8/20; AtomicChat baked 29.6, 0.014, 20/20; nokeepai merged 29.0, 0.042, 20/20; nokeepai LoRA 27.0, 0.043, 19/20; AtomicChat LoRA 21.4, 0.013, 20/20. Codeeval 8/8 on all five.
inkling-2-mini-uncensored-flags-light.png
Which file, which flags: VARIANT=atomicchat (AD-Q4_K, 16.5 GB, 29.6 tok/s decode, 137 prefill) is the default; nokeepai-merged (IQ4_NL plus merge, 29.0 / 146) is nokeepai at full speed; nokeepai (IQ4_NL plus LoRA, 27.0 / 144) needs no merge step; atomicchat-lora (21.4 / 136) is slow, use the baked file; base (IQ4_NL, 29.0 / 145) is the control. The flags are the base recipe's layout with only -ub 96 new: -ngl 99 -ot 'blk\.([0-5]|1[89]|2[0-3])\.ffn_.*_exps=CPU' --fit off -c 65536 -ub 96 -b 2048 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -t 6.

The lever is the GGUF's own MTP head:
--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2
It only fits at 128k with q8_0 KV.

Speed follows acceptance. One thinking answer ran at 20.7, and a prose prompt at 39% acceptance ran 22.6 vs 24.3 plain. Coding gains most.

Nothing above 256k fits. Greedy MTP output matches plain on 3/8 prompts (thinking off); the rest diverges but stays coherent.

sensenova-loop-9b-results-light.png
Results card: SenseNova-Loop-9B, a looped 9B hybrid whose layers 4–27 run twice, on a 12 GB RTX 3060 at 128k context. Decode with thinking off goes from 24.4 tok/s plain to 31.7 with MTP n=2, +30%. Thinking on 24.3 to 33.5, +38%, with one sample as low as 20.7. The 256k long profile finds 3/3 needles at 248k but takes 552 s to the first token. The uncensored Q6_K answers 20 of 20 borderline prompts against 4 of 20 for the default. Prefill on an 8k prompt 857 to 829; 10,586 MiB on the card.
sensenova-loop-9b-flags-light.png
Which profile: ./serve.sh runs 128k with q8_0 K/V and MTP n=2 at 31.7 tok/s, needles 3/3 at 124k; VARIANT=uncensored runs 128k q8_0 with no speculation at 22.2, needles 3/3 at 124k; SNL_PROFILE=long runs 256k q4_0 with no speculation at 24.3, needles 3/3 at 248k; SNL_PROFILE=stock lets fit pick the window at f16 K/V, 24.4, needles not run. The abliterated Q6_K has no MTP head. Default launch line: -ngl 99 --fit off -c 131072 -ub 512 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2 --jinja --reasoning on, 31.7 / 33.5 tok/s thinking off / on. Needs llama.cpp PR #32588; SNL_MMPROJ=auto adds image input.

Thread

1/ (main post) · 250 / 280
Qwen3.8-27B on a 12 GB RTX 3060, stock llama.cpp.

Stock flags: 7.9 tok/s. Tuned: 16.6 tok/s at 32k context, 2.1×. 19.7 tok/s at 16k with every weight on the GPU.

Attach: qwen38-27b-family-video-light-16x9.mp4 (or -dark-16x9; the -9x16 cuts are for phone-first feeds)

2/ · 270 / 280
The files are 10.4–12.2 GB, so something has to sit in RAM, and every GB there costs ~29 ms per token. So shrink everything else on the card:

-ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0
-ub 256
-ot 'blk\.(0|1|2)\.ffn_(up|gate|down)=CPU'

Stock keeps 16 whole layers in RAM. This keeps 0.29 GB.

Attach: qwen38-27b-family-flags-light.png

3/ · 230 / 280
Same flags on all four, decode at 32k, stock → tuned:

pi-adapted 7.9 → 16.6
Huihui abliterated 9.9 → 20.8
DaisyRose-27B 8.0 → 14.4
Heretic 7.0 → 11.6

128k works too: 7.5 tok/s, 5.6 at 120k deep, needles 3/3 at 65k and 123k.

Attach: qwen38-27b-family-results-light.png (or qwen38-27b-family-poster-light.png / -poster-dark.png)

4/ · 277 / 280
MTP: tested, not kept. The head drafts well (91–98% accepted), but it needs ~650 MiB of VRAM, which pushes 6–10 more FFN layers to RAM. Best case +1.8% at 16k, inside the noise, with 12% slower prefill.

The DFlash2 drafter from @CaryPalmerr's Kintsugi-27B does not fit at all.

Alt text

qwen38-27b-family-results-light.png
Results card: Qwen3.8-27B on a 12 GB RTX 3060. The pi-adapted finetune decodes at 7.9 tok/s with stock llama.cpp flags and 16.6 tok/s tuned at 32k context, 2.1×, and 19.7 tok/s at 16k with everything on the GPU. Four finetunes on the same config: pi-adapted 16.6 (2.1×), Huihui 20.8 (2.1×), DaisyRose 14.4 (1.8×), Heretic 11.6 (1.7×).
qwen38-27b-family-flags-light.png
Flags card: four changes to stock llama.cpp take decode from 7.9 to 16.6 tok/s. -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 cuts the K/V cache from 2,048 to 576 MiB; -ub 256 cuts the compute buffer from 269 to 220 MiB; -ot 'blk\.(0|1|2)\.ffn_(up|gate|down)=CPU' leaves 0.29 GB in RAM; -ngl 99 --fit off -c 32768 passes needles 3/3. A strip of 64 layers shows stock keeping 16 whole layers in RAM and the tuned config keeping only the FFN of layers 0 to 2. MTP not kept: 91–98% of drafts accepted, but it needs about 650 MiB; 16.03 tok/s with it vs 16.45 and 16.66 without.
qwen38-27b-family-poster-light.png / qwen38-27b-family-poster-dark.png
Poster: Qwen3.8-27B on a 12 GB RTX 3060, pi-adapted at 32k: 7.9 to 16.6 tok/s, 2.1×. Four finetunes, stock to tuned: pi-adapted 7.9 to 16.6, Huihui 9.9 to 20.8, DaisyRose 8.0 to 14.4, Heretic 7.0 to 11.6. By window: 19.7 tok/s at 16k, 16.6 at 32k, 7.5 at 128k, needles 3/3 in every window.
Video (all four cuts)
28-second video. Qwen3.8-27B on a 12 GB RTX 3060 goes from 7.9 to 16.6 tok/s, 2.1×, and 19.7 at 16k. A strip of 64 layers shows stock flags keeping 16 whole layers in RAM and the tuned config keeping only 0.29 GB of FFN there, at about 29 ms per token per GB. Then the four flags, the four finetunes (pi-adapted 16.6, Huihui 20.8, DaisyRose 14.4, Heretic 11.6 tok/s), the 16k / 32k / 128k windows with needles 3/3, MTP not kept, and the serve commands.

The lever: all routed experts in RAM, hot ones in llama.cpp's MoE cache on the card.

--cpu-moe --moe-cache-mib N

Same VRAM, q8_0 KV: 12 MoE layers pinned 39.6 tok/s, as a 4800 MiB cache 52.7, +33%. The default keeps 1900 MiB to make room for f16 KV and -ub 1024.

q8_0 KV saves VRAM but is slow deep in the window on this card: at 32k, 22.1 tok/s vs 34.1 with f16. f16 wins from about 4k tokens, so it is the default.

Prefill: --load-mode none +38%, -ub 1024 +58% for 2.7% less decode.

5Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B

measured, not posted 6 posts · repo folder nemotron-bolt-e4b/

Verify before posting
  • The link in post 6 points at tree/main/nemotron-bolt-e4b. The repo davidghatley/3060-recipes is public, but nemotron-bolt-e4b/ is only on the local branch trending-batch-1, which is not pushed. The link 404s until the branch is merged to main and pushed.
  • Drafter licence: the DFlash drafter's GGUF metadata names the NVIDIA Software and Model Evaluation License, while the model is OpenMDW-1.1. The whole thread promotes the default profile, which loads that drafter. The owner must decide whether promoting it is fine (if not, the thread would have to lead with nospec, 77.6 tok/s, and drop the speed-up). The package does not mention the licence; the README does.

Stills tap to enlarge

Thread

1/ (main post) · 277 / 280
Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B (NVIDIA, Gemma-4-E4B base) in VRAM on a 12 GB RTX 3060, stock llama.cpp.

Card's command → + NVIDIA's DFlash drafter, tok/s:
thinking on 75.9 → 190.4 (2.5×)
thinking off 76.3 → 216.7 (2.8×)
at 60k 54.2 → 157.8 (2.9×)

4 users × 32k: 270.7 tok/s total.

Attach: nemotron-bolt-e4b-video-light-16x9.mp4 (or -dark-16x9; the -9x16 cuts are for phone-first feeds)

2/ · 269 / 280
The lever is speculative decoding. Plain decode is already at 71% of the bandwidth ceiling, so the card's drafter is the one big win:

--spec-type draft-dflash --spec-draft-n-max 7

It accepts 41% of its 7-token drafts, about 3.9 tokens per step. Plus -ub 1024 and -bs.

Attach: nemotron-bolt-e4b-flags-light.png

3/ · 263 / 280
The price is prefill: the drafter reads the whole prompt too.
8k prompt 4,890 → 3,031 tok/s (0.62×)
61k prompt, first token 19.8 → 30.9 s

For long prompts with short answers, NB_PROFILE=nospec drops the drafter: 5,060 tok/s at 8k, first token at 61k in 18.0 s.

Attach: nemotron-bolt-e4b-results-light.png

4/ · 277 / 280
Checks and limits:
- needles 3/3 at 61k on every profile; 4 × 30k at once on multi
- q8_0 K/V is 22% slower at 32k here, so f16 stays
- KLD not measured (no reference file)
- drafter acceptance measured on code-heavy prompts; chat may accept less
- -bs is experimental upstream

nemotron-bolt-e4b-results-light.png
Results card: Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B, NVIDIA's model on a Gemma-4-E4B base, Q4_K_M 6.18 GB, all in VRAM on a 12 GB RTX 3060. Decode with thinking on goes from 75.9 tok/s with the model card's command to 190.4 with NVIDIA's DFlash drafter, 2.5×. Thinking off 76.3 to 216.7 (2.8×), at 60k context 54.2 to 157.8 (2.9×). The price: prefill at 8k drops from 4,890 to 3,031 tok/s (0.62×). 4 users at 32k each: 270.7 tok/s total; needles 3/3 at 61k; the nospec profile prefills 5,060 tok/s at 8k; 8.6 GB on the card.
nemotron-bolt-e4b-flags-light.png
Which flags: --spec-type draft-dflash (the card's drafter) takes decode with thinking on from 76.2 to 182.7 tok/s, 2.4×; -ub 1024 takes prefill at 8k from 4,899 to 5,060, +3.3%; -bs (backend sampling, experimental upstream) adds 1.5 to 5% with identical greedy output; f16 K/V stays because q8_0 is 22% slower at 32k (48.3 vs 62.2). The default launch line: -ngl 999 -c 65536 -np 1 -ub 1024 -fa on -ctk f16 -ctv f16 -bs --spec-draft-model, --spec-type draft-dflash --spec-draft-n-max 7 --spec-draft-ngl 999 --jinja --reasoning on; 190.4 tok/s and 3,031 prefill at 8k. NB_PROFILE=nospec drops the drafter for 5,060 prefill at 8k.
nemotron-bolt-e4b-poster-light.png / nemotron-bolt-e4b-poster-dark.png
Poster: Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B on a 12 GB RTX 3060, NVIDIA's model on a Gemma-4-E4B base, all in VRAM. Decode with thinking on 75.9 to 190.4 tok/s with the DFlash drafter. Card command vs DFlash: thinking on 75.9 vs 190.4 (2.5×), thinking off 76.3 vs 216.7 (2.8×), at 60k 54.2 vs 157.8 (2.9×), prefill at 8k 4,890 vs 3,031 (0.62×). 4 users at 32k: 270.7 tok/s total. Needles 3/3 at 61k on all profiles. Long prompts: the nospec profile prefills 5,060 tok/s at 8k. Not measured: KLD, drafter acceptance on chat.
Video (all four cuts)
28-second video. Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B, all in VRAM on a 12 GB RTX 3060, decodes at 190.4 tok/s with thinking on using NVIDIA's DFlash drafter, against 75.9 with the model card's command (2.5×); 76.3 to 216.7 with thinking off and 54.2 to 157.8 at 60k. Then the drafter: plain decode is already 71% of its 109 tok/s ceiling, and the drafter gives about 3.9 tokens per step. The price: prefill drops to 0.62× (4,890 to 3,031 at 8k; first token at 61k in 30.9 s instead of 19.8 s), with a nospec profile at 5,060. Four users at 32k reach 270.7 tok/s total; 4 × 64k with the drafter runs out of memory. Limits: needles 3/3 at 61k, KLD not measured, acceptance measured on code, -bs experimental.
